claims.text: Inventory filter for in-content ads lets you set how sensitive the content next to your ads can be on Facebook in-stream reels and Facebook Reels. It is a placement-suitability control, and it does not guarantee that every adjacent piece of content matches your brand standards.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: In-content ads covers two things: Facebook in-stream reels, which can appear within publishers' videos, and ads on Facebook Reels, which are banners on Reels content.

evidence.source_title: About Feed and in-content brand safety and suitability controls

claims.text: You choose from three inventory filter settings. Each setting defines which content is included or excluded next to your ads. On Facebook, Instagram and Threads the filters exclude certain videos and Feed content.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: By default you are opted in to Expanded. Content that breaks Meta's Community Standards, such as full nudity or excessive violence, is excluded whichever setting you pick.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: The filter is a control on where delivery can appear, so it restricts eligible inventory. Meta does not guarantee that all content and publishers will align with your own standards.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: You can set brand suitability controls at business or ad account level in the Meta Brand Safety and Suitability Centre. In Ads Manager you can also set them per ad set.

evidence.source_title: About Feed and in-content brand safety and suitability controls

claims.text: Use it when your brand needs tighter control over the organic Facebook in-stream reels and Reels content your ads sit beside, and you want to set that sensitivity level yourself rather than keep the default.

evidence.source_title: About Feed and in-content brand safety and suitability controls

claims.text: Do not rely on it when you need a guarantee. Meta states there is no guarantee that all content and publishers will meet your own brand suitability standards. Also, the feature is rolling out gradually, so you may not see it yet.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: Check language availability for in-content ads before you depend on it in a market. Meta lists those languages on a separate help page, not on the main page.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: Complete your ad as usual. Your settings are then applied.

claims.text: Brand suitability or brand-safety incident rate: if a stricter setting removes content you consider unsuitable, fewer ads may appear beside it. The trade-off is a smaller pool of eligible inventory, which can raise CPM or limit reach and delivery.

evidence.source_title: About inventory filter

claims.text: Cost per result: the filter does not target people, so any change in cost per result would come only from which placements and content you exclude. Compare ad sets with different settings, and treat results as attributed rather than incremental.

relationships.name: Content suitability in Performance Max
relationships.difference: Google's content theme exclusions set an inventory type (Maximum, Moderate, Limited) across YouTube, the Display Network and Google Video Partners. Meta's filter covers Facebook in-stream reels and Reels ads with its own three settings. Google's channel exclusions cannot be applied at ad group or campaign level, whereas Meta's filter can be set per ad set.
relationships.context: Both limit adjacent content by sensitivity level, but the inventories and setting names differ.

evidence.source_title: How to use brand suitability features in Performance Max

relationships.name: Brand safety inventory filters
relationships.difference: Pinterest's documentation describes filters that show what content appears near ads, the exposure level for campaigns and how policies affect those settings. It does not document matching in-content placements or settings, so treat it as related only.
relationships.context: Same broad purpose of controlling adjacent content, on a different platform with different inventory.
